metadata.title: SUBSAFE / Naval Reactors / UK Safety Case — placed into the SuperGoodReason form
metadata.author: Ville Laitila (placement); source frameworks as cited
metadata.purpose: Systematic placement of every substantive thesis from the nuclear-submarine reliability corpus into its most defensible (sector, level) location, so that unoccupied locations become visible as candidate blind spots.
metadata.sourceDocument: Systemic Failure Minimization in High-Complexity, Extreme Environments: Theoretical Frameworks and Engineering Methodologies from Nuclear Submarine Programs
metadata.placementRule: Each item is placed where the model's own level semantics best fit its function, not where its vocabulary superficially matches. A cell may hold many items. Items asserted as principle but carrying no instrument are marked state='asserted'.

states.evidence: Present in the source as an operating mechanism with a means of verification.
states.asserted: Stated as a principle or requirement, but the source supplies no instrument that would implement or measure it.
states.thin: Present, but as a single acknowledgement, a limitation, or a historical instance rather than a standing capability.

provenance.ai: Proposed completion generated by AI analysis against the model form.
provenance.human: Proposed completion requiring human domain judgement or authority.
provenance.co: Proposed completion produced jointly: AI structures the gap, humans supply mandate and evidence.

phi.gloss: instrument → frame → concept → architecture → detail → project → infrastructure

circles.name: Stability
circles.meta: Rules known, environment slow, deviations small, feedback reinforces the current way of operating.

circles.name: Manageable uncertainty
circles.meta: Variation exists but can be modelled; anticipation remains possible.

circles.name: Complexity
circles.meta: Non-linear; a paradigm begins to appear through experience.

circles.name: Independent agency
circles.meta: Mature agency; the paradigm is under conscious consideration.

circles.name: Emergence
circles.meta: New properties arise; success is not guaranteed.

circles.name: Disruption
circles.meta: Pressure-driven transition; structures reorganize; crisis management.

items.title: Platform survival as founding motive
items.text: The convergence of hydrostatic pressure, an onboard reactor, life support and weapons in one hull makes localized anomalies escalate to platform loss. This recognition is the motive that directs the whole inquiry.

items.title: Two objective parameters define the object
items.text: SUBSAFE identifies its object narrowly: watertight integrity to prevent flooding, and flooding recovery to survive unanticipated seawater ingress. Everything else is deliberately not this object.

items.title: Safety purpose set against commercial purpose
items.text: Primary objective is stated as maximum reasonable safety and hazard elimination, explicitly contrasted with throughput optimization, cost control and schedule adherence.

items.title: Empirical evidence as epistemic identity
items.text: Arrogance — acting from assumed intellectual superiority unsupported by physical facts — is countered by requiring empirical evidence for all operational decisions. This fixes what counts as valid knowing.

items.title: ALARP as risk acceptance under consequence
items.text: A risk cannot simply be deemed tolerable; the Duty Holder must demonstrate that further reduction would be grossly disproportionate in cost, time and effort to the safety benefit gained.
items.cite: The Safety Case and ALARP Principles

items.title: Interactive complexity and tight coupling named
items.text: Interactive complexity: components interact in unexpected, unfamiliar, non-linear or opaque sequences. Tight coupling: architectures lacking slack, with time-dependent processes and invariant sequences.
items.cite: Normal Accident Theory and Systemic Vulnerability

items.title: Deductive and inductive reasoning paired
items.text: Fault Tree Analysis is top-down deductive: how component faults, software glitches and human errors combine to produce system failure. Event Tree Analysis is bottom-up inductive: chronological progression after an initiating event.

items.title: SPAR-H nominal HEP adjusted by eight PSFs
items.text: A nominal human error probability is adjusted across eight Performance Shaping Factors — available time, stress, complexity, training, procedure quality, ergonomics, fitness for duty, organizational culture — with a normalization formula when the product exceeds unity.
items.cite: Standardized Plant Analysis Risk-HRA Mathematical Model

items.title: Safety Case: claim → argument → evidence
items.text: A structured living body of arguments connecting explicit claims to engineering arguments supported by an empirical evidence base — fault trees, material stress certifications, hydrostatic test logs. Safety is demonstrated, not assumed from rule compliance.
items.cite: The Safety Case and ALARP Principles

items.title: Defense-in-Depth as doctrine
items.text: Redundant, physically independent barriers between an initiating hazard and catastrophic failure: automatic isolation valves, secondary manual overrides, passive containment, emergency ballast recovery.

items.title: NAT and HRO as competing disciplines
items.text: Normal Accident Theory predicts catastrophe is structurally inevitable in complex tightly-coupled systems. High Reliability Organization theory holds that near-zero failure is achievable through five embedded behaviors. Both are carried as standing doctrine.

items.title: HRA method family: THERP, SPAR-H, CREAM
items.text: Three cognitive model bases carried as doctrine: procedural action-tree decomposition, informational processing split into diagnosis and action, and the Contextual Control Model with four control modes.

items.title: Six generic axioms abstracted for transfer
items.text: Boundary isolation, material traceability and OQE, functional decoupling and slack, technical competence at management interfaces, single-point accountability, human-reliability-centred engineering — stated as transferable to aerospace, energy and cyber-physical domains.

items.title: NASA benchmarks SUBSAFE after Challenger and Columbia
items.text: Core elements of the programme were adopted by another agency after two of its own catastrophic losses — the strongest available evidence of cross-domain relevance.

items.title: Limits of each framework named but not acted on
items.text: PRA relies on historical component data and struggles with unanticipated non-linear interactions. SPAR-H requires subjective expert rating of PSFs and cannot model evolving multi-person crew interaction. Safety cases risk becoming static documentation. Each limit is stated in a table column and none is carried into the axioms.
items.cite: Architectural Taxonomy of Failure Minimization Frameworks

items.title: HRO: reluctance to simplify
items.text: Rejecting crude explanations for operational anomalies and probing deep systemic root causes. Stated as a cultural behavior; no method, trigger or artifact is specified that would produce it.

items.title: Catastrophe as engineered property, not fate
items.text: Catastrophic failure in extreme environments is an engineered property of system architecture and culture rather than an unavoidable operational reality. This is the corpus's central philosophical claim.

items.title: The NAT paradox declared resolved
items.text: Submarine programmes are said to resolve NAT by using HRO principles to break tight coupling and reduce interactive complexity. This escapes Perrow's quadrant for modes inside the boundary; it leaves everything outside it untouched, and the corpus does not say so.

items.title: The boundary defines the System of Interest
items.text: Inside: pressure hull, hull penetrations, sea-connected piping, sea valves, HP ballast blow, emergency depth-control hydraulics. Outside: combat systems, fire control, internal fire suppression, reactor propulsion. The SOI is delimited by explicit enumeration.
items.cite: The SUBSAFE Boundary and Scope Isolation

items.title: Heat-level records as connection to physical reality
items.text: Complete chemical, physical and historical traceability for all pressure-boundary components: heat-level smelting records, continuous assay tracking, physical marking from raw mill to installation.

items.title: Coupling × complexity typology
items.text: A 2×2 view classifying operational domains by interaction complexity and coupling, placing nuclear submarines with nuclear generation and manned spacecraft in the hyper-complex, tightly-coupled cell.

items.title: Quantified system metrics: CDF and LSR
items.text: Core Damage Frequency for reactors and Loss of Submersible Rate for platforms give the system a numerical self-view.

items.title: Governance comparison across six dimensions
items.text: Objective, authority structure, material verification, procedural adherence, operational slack and auditing mechanism, each contrasted against commercial industrial practice.

items.title: OQE governs the model
items.text: Operational authorization is contingent on verifiable Objective Quality Evidence rather than vendor guarantees or administrative sign-offs. Evidence, not assertion, controls what the organization may believe.

items.title: Continuous independent multi-tiered audit
items.text: Auditing is independent, continuous and multi-tiered, contrasted with periodic administrative checks and self-reporting.

items.title: Nuclear Power School and prototype operation
items.text: Intensive engineering training closing the gap between theoretical design intent and real-world execution — the mechanism by which competence becomes communicable and shared.
items.cite: Deep Technical Competence at Decision-Making Levels

items.title: Mandatory annual historical casualty review
items.text: Annual training reviewing Thresher and Scorpion transmits the casualty knowledge base to each new cohort.

items.title: Four certification pillars as replicable configuration
items.text: Design, Material, Fabrication and Testing form a template that can be instantiated on any new hull or after any maintenance period.

items.title: HRO: preoccupation with failure
items.text: Small operational deviations are to be treated as indicators of systemic vulnerability rather than acceptable variance. No collection channel, aggregation method or trend instrument is specified anywhere in the corpus.

items.title: Engineered conservatism and deliberate slack
items.text: High engineered conservatism and deliberate response protocols, contrasted with hyper-optimized lean operations and minimized buffers. Axiom 3 requires physical separation, operational buffers and structural slack in critical workflows.

items.title: HRO: commitment to resilience
items.text: Intrinsic capability to contain, adapt to and recover from unforeseen casualties. Stated as a cultural property with no measure of how much resilience exists or whether it is growing or eroding.

items.title: Anomaly triggers mandatory stop and review
items.text: Any operational anomaly requires immediate plant stabilization, casualty containment and technical review by headquarters engineers before operations resume.
items.cite: Conservative Design and Formality of Operations

items.title: The Thresher threshold, crossed and failed
items.text: Braze failure → seawater spray → electrical shorts → reactor scram → propulsion loss → emergency blow attempted → moisture freezes in the HP air, ice blocks strainers → descent past test depth → hull collapse. 129 fatalities. The adaptation threshold in its literal form.
items.cite: The USS Thresher Casualty and Causal Engineering Mechanics

items.title: Flooding recovery as designed threshold capability
items.text: The second of SUBSAFE's two objective parameters is explicitly the capability to survive the threshold event rather than merely to avoid it.
items.cite: The SUBSAFE Boundary and Scope Isolation

items.title: SUBSAFE created by disruption, 3 June 1963
items.text: The programme was itself produced by a Δψ6 event. It is the only radical-renewal instance in the corpus, it is 62 years old, and it is recorded as history rather than as a standing capability to renew again.

items.title: Pressure hull and penetrations as minimal viable module
items.text: The smallest element below which nothing else can compensate: hull structure and every penetration through it.
items.cite: The SUBSAFE Boundary and Scope Isolation

items.title: Shipyards, contractors and the operating fleet
items.text: The operational units performing primary activity — field offices, shipyards, prime contractors and active fleet operations, all under centralized technical authority.

items.title: Standardized criteria and formal engineering review
items.text: Formal engineering reviews and standardized design criteria coordinate between units and suppress divergence. Operating procedures are simplified, standardized and strictly enforced.
items.cite: Certification Pillars — Design / Formality of Operations

items.title: SUBSAFE certification as operational control
items.text: Certification requires documented objective quality evidence across four domains before the platform may submerge. Control is exercised by withholding authorization.

items.title: Centralized technical authority over the whole chain
items.text: The Director of Naval Reactors maintains centralized technical authority over field offices, shipyards, prime contractors and active fleet operations simultaneously.

items.title: Zero unauthorized variance
items.text: Individual operational deviation from established procedure is strictly prohibited. Strict procedural compliance is contrasted with discretionary operational flexibility.
items.cite: Conservative Design and Formality of Operations

items.title: HRO: deference to expertise — in direct conflict
items.text: Decision authority during emergencies is to be decoupled from formal rank so subject-matter experts at any tier may halt operations. This contradicts zero-variance procedural compliance in the same cell, and the corpus adjudicates neither.

items.title: Unannounced audits and requalification
items.text: Complacency is combated through continuous unannounced audits and rigorous re-qualification regimes — control instruments applied to conformance.

items.title: Dual-agency mission structure
items.text: Naval Reactors combines Department of the Navy and Department of Energy authority, granting control over both military operational requirements and the civilian research laboratories.

items.title: Cradle-to-grave single-point accountability
items.text: Absolute single-point accountability spanning core physics research, plant design, contractor oversight, officer selection, operational procedures, overhaul logistics and decommissioning.

items.title: Duty Holder: named, personal, non-delegable
items.text: Named individuals hold direct legal and operational responsibility for platform safety and cannot delegate it to contractors, suppliers or subordinate agencies.

items.title: Technical competence required to hold authority
items.text: Administrative managers without deep domain expertise are structurally barred from making operational or engineering determinations.
items.cite: Deep Technical Competence at Decision-Making Levels

items.title: Redundant isolation valving
items.text: Redundant isolation valves, automatic isolation, secondary manual overrides — the tool-level instruments of containment.

items.title: Margins prioritized over performance
items.text: Reactor design parameters prioritize safety margins over raw power density or experimental weight savings; piping layouts are conservative. The design frame is set before any solution is chosen.
items.cite: Conservative Design and Formality of Operations

items.title: Fail-safe recovery configurations
items.text: Fail-safe recovery system configurations, including the emergency main ballast tank blow as the designed answer to loss of buoyancy.

items.title: Interfaces designed to hold cognitive control mode
items.text: Display interfaces, alarm hierarchies and procedural drills are structured to keep operators within Strategic or Tactical control modes during high-stress emergencies. Axiom 6 makes this a design requirement.
items.cite: Contextual Cognitive Control via CREAM / Axiom 6

items.title: Boundary isolation as system architecture
items.text: Axiom 1: identify the specific catastrophic failure modes threatening platform survival and isolate those systems inside a strict certification boundary; keep non-critical capability outside to control complexity.

items.title: Physical separation of seawater from vital electrics
items.text: The specific architectural remedy for the Thresher mechanism: strict physical domain separation so that failure in one domain cannot propagate to disable secondary mitigation.

items.title: Silver brazing eliminated; welding automated
items.text: Mandatory process discipline, automated welding, certified operator licensing, and the elimination of the silver-brazed joint type that initiated the Thresher casualty.

items.title: Cost acknowledged as a limitation only
items.text: High capital and administrative overhead is listed in the limitations column. Timing, investment and mandate are never treated as design variables — the only appearance of the project dimension is as a cost complaint.

items.title: UK public regulatory framework
items.text: JSP 430 and the Defence Safety Authority frameworks DSA02-DMR and DSA03, with the Defence Maritime Regulator setting safety regulation across the acquisition cycle. Originating from the Carver Report and Lord Cullen's Piper Alpha inquiry.

items.title: Hydrostatic testing, NDT and sea trials
items.text: Empirically proving structural and operational integrity before deployment and after maintenance: pressure testing beyond test depth, non-destructive ultrasonic inspection, sea trials.

items.title: The individual watchstander under procedure
items.text: Certified operator licensing, individual requalification, and the requirement that the individual execute written protocol without deviation.
items.cite: Conservative Design and Formality of Operations

items.title: Traceability chain from mill to installation
items.text: The material chain implemented as logistics: continuous assay tracking and physical marking following each component from raw mill through fabrication to installation.

items.title: Overhaul and decommissioning named in passing
items.text: Cradle-to-grave responsibility includes overhaul logistics and ultimate decommissioning, and testing is required after maintenance. The life-cycle phase is never read as a variable that changes what the right action is.

items.title: Immediate response: scram and stabilize
items.text: Automated reactor scram on fault; anomaly requires immediate plant stabilization and casualty containment. Feedback at its fastest and most local.

items.title: Zero losses since 1963 — the headline signal
items.text: Between 1915 and 1963 the US Navy lost 16 submarines to non-combat causes. Since SUBSAFE, no certified submarine has been lost. An outcome metric with a decades-long sampling interval, success-only, and protected by the exclusion of Scorpion as not fully certified.

items.title: Headquarters technical review before resumption
items.text: Operations may not resume after an anomaly until headquarters engineers have reviewed it — a two-way loop that adjusts the operating decision.
items.cite: Conservative Design and Formality of Operations

items.title: HRO: sensitivity to operations
items.text: Continuous real-time situational awareness across all operational levels. Stated as a behavior; no artifact, channel or measure is specified.

items.title: Post-casualty conviction: 1963 and 2003
items.text: SUBSAFE after Thresher; NASA's adoption of its elements after Challenger and Columbia. Both are recovery-from-crisis instances, both are historical, and neither is a standing mechanism.

items.title: Anticipatory safety envelope
items.text: Publish a standing statement of the operating conditions the current safety case does NOT cover — new energy storage chemistry, autonomous payloads, printed spares, contested acoustic environments. Purpose at this level must be future-facing; today it is entirely present-tense.
items.why: α5 asks what the system anticipates. The corpus contains no forward-looking purpose statement at all — only present-state conformance.

items.title: What counts as failure other than losing a boat
items.text: Doctrine on long-term direction that names the non-platform failure modes the enterprise can actually suffer: loss of legitimacy, absorption into another authority, industrial-base death, deterrence irrelevance. Δψ4 lists these; α7 must own them.
items.why: α7 is empty. With only 'do not lose a submarine' as purpose, every other way the enterprise can die is invisible to it.

items.title: Researcher-mode α: who is the observer and what is their stake
items.text: The α sector carries two modes in the model — object identity and researcher identity. Every α item in this corpus is object-mode. Name the observing authority's own position, motive and susceptibility to being wrong as an explicit part of the safety case.
items.why: Second-order science requires the observer be in the frame. A safety architecture that never describes its own observer cannot detect observer drift.

items.title: Cross-domain precursor synthesis
items.text: Integrate submarine, naval aviation and civil nuclear precursor data into one causal ontology so that a mechanism first seen in another domain can be recognized here before it arrives. χ5 is the ecosystem of understanding; today each programme learns only from its own casualties.
items.why: χ5 is empty. The corpus's own best example — NASA learning from SUBSAFE — ran one way and only after two disasters.

items.title: Allied exchange at a declassified abstraction layer
items.text: Share failure *mechanisms* — ice formation in rapid gas expansion, seawater-to-electrics propagation geometry — without platform specifics. Collective intelligence is achievable above the classification line even when the evidence beneath it cannot move.
items.why: χ7 is structurally blocked by classification, which is real. But the block applies to particulars, not to mechanisms, and nothing exploits that distinction.

items.title: Devolution watch
items.text: Quantified indicators that distinguish programme development from programme decline: margin erosion rate, qualified-skill pipeline years-of-cover, maintenance deferral trend, time from anomaly to fleet-wide corrective action. Δψ5 asks what survives change and what disappears in decline.
items.why: Δψ5 is empty. Nothing in the architecture can tell the difference between a programme improving and a programme quietly hollowing out.

items.title: Standing synthetic-disruption cell
items.text: A permanent adversarial function whose task is to invent the next casualty mode — not to audit compliance with existing rules. Success criterion: at least one previously unregistered cascade path per cycle. This manufactures the Δψ that the 62-year record has removed.
items.why: Δψ6 holds one item and it is dated 1963. Safety architectures are created by disasters and decay in their absence; nothing here replaces the missing disaster.

items.title: The limits of conservatism
items.text: Doctrine on when risk-aversion itself becomes the hazard: fleet unavailability, deferred modernization, deterrence gaps, an industrial base that atrophies because nothing is ever built differently. Δψ7 warns that permanent disruption and complete stagnation are both destructive.
items.why: Δψ7 is empty. The architecture has an accelerator for caution and no brake on it.

items.title: The missing System 4
items.text: Establish an environment-scanning and future-adaptation function with standing in the governance structure. Its product: a ranked register of forces capable of invalidating a current safety-case assumption, each mapped to the assumption threatened and the pillar that would have to change.
items.why: β5 is the VSM's System 4 and it is empty, while β4 (System 3) holds six items. The model's own failure note reads: 'If development capacity is missing, the system remains efficient in the present but becomes blind to future change.'

items.title: Ethical regulator: who pays for adaptation
items.text: A standing authority empowered to ask whose reserves are being consumed when operational pressure rises — crew rest, shipyard workforce, maintenance margin, host-community risk. Δψ2's emancipatory question, given an organizational home.
items.why: β7 is empty. Buffer consumption is currently invisible because nobody owns the question of who is paying for it.

items.title: Interface Duty Holder and Cascade Path Register
items.text: Named ownership, with full Duty Holder liability, for every propagation route that crosses a certification boundary. Deliverable: a register enumerating each cascade path, the authority on both sides, and a joint-availability argument for any two recovery paths a single event could disable. A path with no owner on both sides is itself a reportable defect.
items.why: τ4 is empty and load-bearing. The Thresher cascade crossed the post-1963 boundaries four times. The model's τ4 failure note: 'the chain breaks between services even when each part works locally.'

items.title: The industrial base as a certified system
items.text: Apply Axiom 2 to human capital: qualified-welder headcount, age distribution, pipeline throughput, attrition and years-of-margin per critical skill, reported at the same cadence and to the same authority as material nonconformance.
items.why: τ5 is empty. A valve can be traced to the heat it was smelted from; nobody can state how many qualified pressure-boundary welders exist or how long the pipeline holds.

items.title: Decommissioning and ocean environment inside the same worldview
items.text: Spent fuel, hull disposal and long-term marine impact treated as part of the safety practice rather than as a separate programme with a separate authority. τ7 asks whether action contradicts the worldview it claims to serve.
items.why: τ7 is empty. Cradle-to-grave ownership is asserted at β6 but has no implementation layer at the worldview scale.

items.title: Non-punitive precursor channel
items.text: A negotiated reporting system for near-misses, self-correcting excursions, procedures followed but assessed as wrong, and drills that only just succeeded — aggregated, trended and reported alongside material nonconformance. Protection must be structural, not cultural.
items.why: Ω3 is empty, and without it HRO's 'preoccupation with failure' at Δψ1 has no instrument. The principle is stated three times in the corpus and implemented nowhere.

items.title: Where overruled dissent goes
items.text: A defined route for concerns the technical authority rejects: who records them, what evidence would reopen them, and who revisits them on a schedule. Ω5 is reconciliation after disappointment — the feedback that only exists if someone was told no.
items.why: Ω5 is empty. In a strict single-point-authority structure, the rejected concern is exactly the signal most likely to have been right and least likely to survive.

items.title: Audit the standard, not the conformance
items.text: A periodic second-order review whose question is whether the certification criteria still describe the hazard — not whether the platform conforms to them. The observer, the model and the feedback process enter the inquiry together.
items.why: Ω6 is empty and it is the deepest gap. Complacency is not a character flaw here; it is the structural consequence of fighting complacency with object-mode instruments only. Every audit in the corpus checks conformance to a standard nothing ever re-examines.

items.title: Margin telemetry as the collective record
items.text: Replace the zero-loss headline with a fleet-wide distribution of distance-to-limit for every safety-critical function — blow-system mass flow against requirement, penetration wall thickness against minimum, valve closure time — trended, with alarms on drift of the adverse tail rather than on individual failures.
items.why: Ω7 is empty and Ω1 carries an outcome metric that cannot inform. A fleet whose 5th-percentile blow margin has fallen 15% in a decade currently reports as fully certified, zero losses.

items.title: Circle 1 → Circle 6 transition protocol
items.text: A formally declared off-nominal regime with explicit entry criteria, a named declaring authority, an announcement obligation, a duty to reason aloud, and post-hoc protection so that correct entry is never itself a finding. It must govern all eight roles — what counts as evidence and who decides also change in a crisis, not only what is done.
items.why: The architecture is natively Circle 1: rules known, deviations small, feedback reinforcing. Casualties are natively Circle 6. No transition between the two regimes is defined anywhere, and procedural absolutism forbids the very control mode a novel casualty requires.

items.title: Correlated, scenario-conditioned HRA
items.text: Replace independent PSF rating with joint PSF states per casualty archetype, elicited from observed drill performance. State the correlation assumption on the face of every human error probability quoted.
items.why: π6 holds the limitation as an acknowledgement only. PSFs are causally chained — time collapse drives stress drives complexity drives procedure invalidity — so a multiplicative independent model underestimates error probability worst in exactly the compound casualties that end platforms.

items.title: Untestable Function Register
items.text: Every safety function whose full-condition validation is impossible, listed with the delta between test and casualty conditions, the physics that could differ across it, and the compensating evidence claimed. Rule: an untestable function must have a redundant path that fails on different physics.
items.why: Thresher's blow system failed on unmodeled thermodynamics under conditions only present in the emergency. Emergency systems are exercised only in emergencies, so their failure modes are the least observed — and the four pillars presume testability.

tensions.finding: Boundary isolation reduces complexity inside each boundary and concentrates residual risk at the boundaries, where nobody is the Duty Holder.
The structure represents only one of the two goods the enterprise pursues; the unrepresented one — availability — is not eliminated, only made invisible.
The fact base consists of outcomes, not margins. A sixty-year-rare event cannot be managed from outcome data.
The feedback loop runs in months to years; software and cyber threat modes mutate in days. Ω slower than Δψ is unstable by construction.
PRA requires historical component data; novel and informational failure modes have none, so the quantitative apparatus is blind exactly at the frontier.
Procedural absolutism maximizes safety for anticipated casualties and reduces it for unanticipated ones — the class that ends platforms.
Deference to expertise and strict procedural compliance are contradictory instructions issued to the same watchstander at the same moment.
Maximal structural rigidity plus zero change-detection means the architecture's fitness can only decline, and never be observed declining.
Purpose is stated only in object mode and feedback returns only to the object; neither ever examines the observing authority itself.
Every framework limitation is named in a table column and none is carried forward into the axioms that the corpus actually proposes.

triads.name: The interface triad
triads.finding: Structure draws the boundary, implementation crosses it, feedback never observes the crossing. All three gaps — β5, τ4, Ω6 — sit on this triangle, which is why the Thresher pattern is still reachable.

triads.name: The drift triad
triads.finding: A single-valued purpose plus an undetected change pressure plus a rigid structure is the classic migration-to-the-boundary geometry: every named role discharges its duty perfectly while the enterprise drifts.

triads.name: The evidence triad
triads.finding: Evidence collection is exceptional at levels 1–3, theory is strong at 3–5, and feedback never closes the loop back onto either. The corpus can prove the hull conforms; it cannot prove the standard still describes the sea.
